newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU export bids support French barley.
newsitem.headline: EU export bids support French barley.

text.p: French barley remained at its highest level for the 1996/97 campaign on Thursday as operators eagerly await the outcome of this week's grain auction, dealers said.
Rouen barley for April-June delivery was quoted at 890 francs per tonne, excluding carry, unchanged on Wednesday.
"Barley is the star today. We are expecting export rebates," one dealer said.
In France exporters bid to export 233,000 tonnes of free-market barley at rebates ranging from 23.68 to 26.43 Ecus per tonne.
Exporters said there was still business to cover following recent sales to Iran, Cyprus and Libya and an earlier deal with Saudi Arabia.
Further support also came from concern the EU might decide to extend to barley from soft wheat its decision to close weekly export tenders for 1996/97, some dealers said.

French domestic grains are traded on a "July basis," reflecting their underlying value without the twice-monthly carrying charges which must also be added for delivery periods between August 1 and the end of the July/June crop year.
